Abstract:

Titanium dioxide (TiO₂) nanomaterials due to the excellent physicochemical properties, chemical stability, biocompatibility and tunable surface characteristics attracted considerable attention in biomedical research. This study focuses on the development of nanocomposite of carbon nanorods-titanium dioxide (CNR-TiO2) for uric acid detection. First, CNR was synthesised with a low temperature hydrothermal method. The characterization of the synthesized materials is performed with X-ray diffraction (XRD), Fourier Transforms Infrared, Raman Spectroscopy, Scanning Electron Microscopy. Structural analyses of XRD gives the most intense diffraction peak at approximately 2&theta = 34.8&deg. FTIR surface chemistry peak indicates the presence of oxygen- and carbon-containing functional groups around 3778 cm-1 corresponds to the O&ndashH stretching vibration and 1593 cm⁻&sup1 corresponds to C=C stretching vibration and the absorption band at 1440 cm⁻&sup1 attributes to C&ndashH bending vibrations. Dynamic light scattering (DLS) analysis revealed a average hydrodynamic diameter of 1317 nm, while zeta potential of &minus23.1 &plusmn 4.13 mV that the synthesised CNR possesses moderate colloidal stability. Future work will focus on the synthesis of TiO₂ nanoparticles and TiO₂/CNR nanocomposites and the subsequent development of biosensor. The developed CNR&ndashTiO₂ nanocomposite will undergo evaluation of its potential to enhance the electrochemical sensing performance of uric acid, with particular emphasis on improving sensitivity, selectivity, and detection efficiency.
